title: Vaginal bleeding in pregnancy
summary: Any bleeding from the genital tract in pregnancy, before onset of labour.

openingFields.label: Known risk factors (e.g. known low-lying placenta/praevia, previous caesarean, anticoagulants, trauma)

vb-01.text: Are there any signs of significant blood loss or shock — feeling faint or dizzy, rapid heartbeat, clammy skin, confusion, or collapse?
vb-01.phoneText: Ask: does she feel faint, dizzy, or like she might pass out? Is her heart racing?

answers.label: Yes — signs of shock or collapse

citation.section: GTG 63 — Antepartum Haemorrhage, and MBRRACE-UK red-flag maternal collapse priority

vb-early-01.text: Is there severe or worsening one-sided abdominal pain, pain at the tip of the shoulder, or pain that seems out of proportion to the amount of bleeding?
vb-early-01.phoneText: Ask: is the pain mainly on one side, or does she have any pain right up at the shoulder tip?

citation.section: Ectopic pregnancy and miscarriage — presenting symptoms of ectopic pregnancy

vb-early-02.text: How much bleeding — spotting, similar to a period, or heavier with clots?

vb-early-03.text: Any fever, offensive-smelling discharge, or (if already examined) an open cervix?

vb-aph-01.text: Is there constant, severe abdominal pain, a tense/'woody' hard uterus, or does the bleeding seem less than you'd expect given the pain or degree of shock (possible concealed abruption)?
vb-aph-01.phoneText: Ask: is the pain constant and severe, not coming and going? Does her tummy feel very hard or tense?

citation.section: GTG 63 — Antepartum Haemorrhage, placental abruption features

vb-aph-02.text: Is a low-lying placenta or placenta praevia already known from previous scans?

vb-aph-03.text: How much bleeding — spotting/light, or heavier (soaking pads, clots)?

vb-aph-04.text: Any contractions, reduced fetal movements, or other concerns?

vb-outcome-red-shock.title: Suspected major obstetric haemorrhage / maternal shock
actions: Call 999 / put out an emergency call per local major obstetric haemorrhage protocol.
Do not perform a digital vaginal examination — placenta praevia has not been excluded.
Prepare for emergency transfer/resuscitation: IV access, bloods including group & save/crossmatch, senior obstetric and anaesthetic input.
See the Major haemorrhage emergency drill for full actions.
vb-outcome-red-shock.phoneScript: Tell her to call 999 now — do not drive herself. Say clearly: significant bleeding in pregnancy with feeling faint/dizzy needs an emergency ambulance.
documentationPrompts: Time bleeding started and estimated volume.
Vital signs and level of consciousness.
Time of emergency call and response.

citations.section: GTG 52 — Prevention and Management of Postpartum Haemorrhage / GTG 63 — Antepartum Haemorrhage
Maternal mortality reports — haemorrhage as a leading direct cause of death

vb-outcome-red-ectopic.title: Suspected ectopic pregnancy
actions: Arrange emergency transfer for assessment — do not wait for a routine early pregnancy unit slot.
If any signs of shock/collapse develop at any point, call 999 immediately.
Early pregnancy unit or gynaecology emergency assessment with urgent ultrasound and beta-hCG.
vb-outcome-red-ectopic.phoneScript: Tell her this needs to be checked as an emergency today — advise her to go straight to the emergency department or call 999 if the pain is severe, she feels faint, or symptoms worsen on the way.
safetyNetting: Call 999 immediately if pain becomes severe, she feels faint/dizzy, or she collapses.
documentationPrompts: Gestation / last menstrual period if known.
Advice given and route of referral.

citations.section: Ectopic pregnancy and miscarriage — presenting symptoms and emergency referral

vb-outcome-red-abruption.title: Suspected placental abruption
actions: Call 999 / emergency obstetric response per local major obstetric haemorrhage / abruption protocol.
Continuous fetal monitoring as soon as available; anticipate fetal compromise.
IV access, bloods including group & save/crossmatch and clotting, senior obstetric and anaesthetic input.
Do not perform a digital vaginal examination until placenta praevia excluded.
vb-outcome-red-abruption.phoneScript: Tell her to call 999 now — severe constant tummy pain with bleeding in pregnancy is an emergency and needs an ambulance, not a car journey if she is deteriorating.
documentationPrompts: Estimated blood loss (may be much less than actual loss if concealed).
Fetal movements and (once available) fetal heart status.
Time of emergency call and response.

vb-outcome-orange-early-heavy.title: Heavier early-pregnancy bleeding — possible miscarriage
vb-outcome-orange-early-heavy.target: Seen within 15 minutes (face-to-face) / same-day emergency gynae or EPU assessment (phone)
actions: Arrange same-day early pregnancy unit (or emergency gynaecology if EPU closed) assessment with ultrasound.
Check observations; escalate immediately if any signs of shock develop.
Offer information sensitively — outcome is uncertain at this stage.
vb-outcome-orange-early-heavy.phoneScript: Tell her this needs checking today at the early pregnancy unit. If bleeding becomes heavy (soaking a pad an hour or more) or she feels faint, she should call 999 or go straight to A&E.
safetyNetting: Call 999 or attend A&E immediately if bleeding becomes heavy/soaking, or if she feels faint, dizzy, or unwell.
Return/call again if pain worsens or fever develops.

citations.section: Ectopic pregnancy and miscarriage — early pregnancy unit referral

vb-outcome-orange-early-infection.title: Early pregnancy bleeding with possible infection
actions: Arrange same-day assessment — early pregnancy unit or emergency gynaecology.
Consider sepsis screen (NEWS2/MEOWS observations, temperature, HR, BP, RR) — see Sepsis emergency drill if she appears unwell.
Ultrasound and clinical assessment for suspected infected miscarriage.
vb-outcome-orange-early-infection.phoneScript: Tell her this needs checking today because of the fever/discharge — advise her to come in now, and to call 999 if she starts to feel very unwell, shivery, or confused.
safetyNetting: Call 999 if she develops shivering, confusion, rapid breathing, or feels very unwell — these can be signs of sepsis.

citations.section: Ectopic pregnancy and miscarriage — infection risk
Sepsis — recognition and early management, pregnancy-specific red flags

vb-outcome-green-early.title: Light early-pregnancy bleeding, no red-flag features
vb-outcome-green-early.target: Non-urgent — routine EPU referral with safety-netting
actions: Arrange routine early pregnancy unit assessment (timing per local EPU pathway).
Advise rest and to avoid intercourse/tampons until reviewed — VERIFY local advice wording.
vb-outcome-green-early.phoneScript: Explain that light spotting is common and often settles, but it does need checking at the early pregnancy unit. Come back to us straight away, any time, if bleeding gets heavier, pain starts, or she feels unwell.
safetyNetting: Attend immediately if bleeding becomes heavier, pain develops (especially one-sided), or she feels faint or unwell.

citations.section: Ectopic pregnancy and miscarriage — routine EPU pathway

vb-outcome-orange-praevia.title: Bleeding with known low-lying placenta / praevia
actions: Admit for assessment — do NOT perform a digital vaginal examination.
Continuous or intermittent fetal monitoring as clinically indicated; maternal observations.
Urgent obstetric review; ultrasound to reassess placental position/bleeding source if not recently done.
Group & save/crossmatch per local major obstetric haemorrhage protocol given known praevia.
vb-outcome-orange-praevia.phoneScript: Because of her low-lying placenta, tell her to come in now for assessment. If bleeding becomes heavy or she feels faint, she must call 999 instead.
safetyNetting: Call 999 immediately if bleeding becomes heavy, pain develops, or she feels faint or unwell.
documentationPrompts: Known placental position and gestation at last scan.

citations.section: GTG 63 — Antepartum Haemorrhage, placenta praevia — avoid digital examination

vb-outcome-orange-aph-heavy.title: Heavier antepartum bleeding (24+ weeks)
actions: Admit for assessment — do not perform digital vaginal examination until placenta praevia excluded by scan/notes.
Continuous fetal monitoring (CTG) once available; maternal observations.
Group & save/crossmatch, urgent obstetric review, ultrasound.
Consider speculum examination by an appropriately experienced clinician once praevia excluded, to assess for local causes.
vb-outcome-orange-aph-heavy.phoneScript: Tell her to come in now, this needs checking and monitoring today. Call 999 instead if bleeding is very heavy or she feels faint.
safetyNetting: Call 999 if bleeding becomes very heavy, pain worsens, or she feels faint/unwell.

vb-outcome-orange-aph-other.title: Antepartum bleeding with contractions, reduced movements, or other concerns
actions: Admit for assessment — do not perform digital vaginal examination until placenta praevia excluded.
CTG and maternal observations.
Urgent obstetric review — assess for labour, abruption, or other cause alongside the presenting concern.
vb-outcome-orange-aph-other.phoneScript: Tell her to come in now — with the bleeding and [contractions/reduced movements], this needs checking together today.
safetyNetting: Call 999 if bleeding becomes heavy, pain is severe/constant, or she feels faint or unwell.

vb-outcome-yellow-aph-light.title: Light antepartum bleeding (24+ weeks), no other concerns
actions: Arrange same-day assessment — do not perform digital vaginal examination until placenta praevia excluded.
CTG, maternal observations, and obstetric review.
Speculum examination once praevia excluded, to look for a local cause if appropriate.
vb-outcome-yellow-aph-light.phoneScript: Tell her this still needs checking today, even though the bleeding is light — please come in so we can monitor the baby and check for a cause.
safetyNetting: Come in immediately, any time, if bleeding becomes heavier, pain starts, movements reduce, or she feels unwell.
